metadata.title: RDS MySQL Upgrade Assistant - Threat Model

businessContext.description: RDS MySQL Upgrade Assistant - Open-source CLI tool and MCP server automating batch Blue/Green deployment upgrades for Amazon RDS MySQL 8.0 to 8.4.

components.name: Shell Scripts (AWS CLI)
components.description: 11 bash scripts for RDS operations and mysql client for database connectivity

components.name: MCP Server (Python/FastMCP)
components.description: Python FastMCP subprocess wrapper exposing shell scripts as MCP tools via stdio

components.name: Amazon RDS MySQL
components.description: Target RDS MySQL 8.0 instances and Multi-AZ DB Clusters being upgraded to 8.4

components.name: AWS Secrets Manager
components.description: Stores database credentials retrieved by scripts for MySQL connectivity

components.name: AWS IAM
components.description: Authentication for AWS CLI calls and optional IAM database authentication

components.name: Kiro IDE/CLI
components.description: AI-powered IDE/CLI communicating with MCP server via stdio for natural language upgrade orchestration

connections.description: Kiro communicates with MCP server via local stdio pipe
MCP server invokes shell scripts as local subprocesses
Shell scripts manage RDS instances via AWS API
Shell scripts connect to MySQL for prechecks and validation
Shell scripts retrieve database credentials from Secrets Manager
Shell scripts authenticate via IAM for AWS CLI calls

threats.threat_source: An attacker with local process access on the developer workstation
threats.prerequisites: with ability to intercept or modify MCP stdio communication
threats.threat_action: inject malicious tool calls through the MCP stdio pipe
threats.threat_impact: unauthorized RDS operations executed through the MCP server

threats.threat_source: An operator misconfiguring batch upgrade parameters
threats.prerequisites: with access to batch configuration files
threats.threat_action: configure high concurrency targeting all instances simultaneously
threats.threat_impact: simultaneous downtime across multiple production databases

threats.threat_source: A malicious operator performing unauthorized upgrades
threats.prerequisites: when upgrade scripts lack comprehensive audit logging
threats.threat_action: perform destructive operations without traceable audit trail
threats.threat_impact: inability to attribute or investigate unauthorized database modifications

threats.threat_source: An operator or attacker with access to script debug output
threats.prerequisites: when bash debug mode (set -x) is enabled during execution
threats.threat_action: capture credentials from debug trace output when retrieving secrets
threats.threat_impact: exposure of database passwords and IAM auth tokens in log output

threats.threat_source: A malicious insider or attacker with filesystem access
threats.prerequisites: with write access to the script directory on the execution host
threats.threat_action: modify shell scripts to inject malicious commands during upgrade
threats.threat_impact: unauthorized modification or deletion of production RDS instances

threats.threat_source: A local user or attacker on the execution host
threats.prerequisites: with access to process listing or shell history on the host
threats.threat_action: observe database credentials passed via -p CLI argument in ps or history
threats.threat_impact: exposure of database credentials enabling unauthorized access

threats.threat_source: An attacker with access to script output or log files
threats.prerequisites: when error handling exposes raw AWS API responses
threats.threat_action: trigger errors to extract AWS account details from error messages
threats.threat_impact: disclosure of AWS account IDs and ARNs aiding reconnaissance

threats.threat_source: A network-level attacker with a rogue CA certificate
threats.prerequisites: with network position to perform MITM on MySQL connections
threats.threat_action: intercept MySQL connections using ssl-mode=REQUIRED without CA pinning
threats.threat_impact: credential theft or data interception during precheck queries

threats.threat_source: An attacker who can modify batch configuration files
threats.prerequisites: with ability to modify YAML config files for batch_upgrade.sh
threats.threat_action: inject malicious values into batch config YAML parsed by shell
threats.threat_impact: command injection or unintended operations on RDS instances

threats.threat_source: An authorized user with excessive IAM permissions
threats.prerequisites: with IAM credentials that have overly broad RDS permissions
threats.threat_action: use upgrade scripts to modify or delete RDS instances beyond scope
threats.threat_impact: unauthorized upgrade, modification, or deletion of production databases

mitigations.content: Enforce TLS via --ssl-mode=REQUIRED for all MySQL connections. RDS CA bundle available for VERIFY_IDENTITY upgrade.
Sanitize error messages — no raw AWS API output exposed. Generic guidance shown without ARNs, account IDs, or internal API details.
Validate all inputs via regex — instance IDs, version numbers, ports, regions, hostnames. Reject unexpected characters.
Use AWS Secrets Manager (--secret-id) or IAM database auth (--iam). Credentials written to --defaults-extra-file with umask 077 and unset from memory.
Batch orchestrator enforces configurable concurrency limits (default: 3). Precheck gating skips instances with errors. Dry-run mode validates before execution.
IAM least-privilege policies in docs/iam-policies.json — separate ReadOnly, Upgrade, and ParameterGroup roles with region-scoped conditions.
Audit logging via scripts/lib/audit_log.sh — logs user, timestamp, AWS caller identity, operation, instance ID, and exit code to logs/ directory with 700 permissions.
Script integrity verification via scripts/lib/integrity_check.sh + CHECKSUMS.sha256. SHA-256 checksums for all scripts. Dependency version verification.
